Add opt-in duplicate-key rejection to this real python-dotenv repository. A deployment service must reject ambiguous configuration before changing its process environment, while existing callers keep the current last-value-wins behavior. Add a keyword-only strict: bool = False parameter to dotenv_values(), load_dotenv(), and the existing DotEnv constructor. Preserve all existing positional arguments and defaults. Validate strict as an actual bool, rejecting other types with TypeError before file discovery, path conversion, stream reads or environment changes. This validation also applies when loading is disabled. With a valid strict option, PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED continues to disable load_dotenv without opening or reading configuration. dotenv_values retains its existing independent behavior.

Export DuplicateKeyError from the top-level dotenv package as a ValueError subclass. It exposes key: str, first_line: int and second_line: int, using one-based physical start lines of the first and duplicate valid bindings. Its human-readable message identifies the key and those line numbers, without including either value. In strict mode, two valid parsed bindings with the same decoded key raise this error, even when values are identical, either occurrence is a bare key with no value, or one binding uses export or a quoted key. Report the first duplicate encountered in file order and preserve the original first occurrence location when a key appears more than twice. Comments, blank lines and invalid parser bindings do not define keys; retain existing invalid-line warnings. A quoted multiline value counts all its physical lines, but its binding location is its starting line.

Duplicate detection precedes interpolation and, for load_dotenv, all os.environ writes. If a duplicate is found, no newly parsed key is installed and no existing environment value is changed, regardless of override or interpolate. Never cache a partial dictionary after a parse failure. Preserve existing interpolation ordering, environment precedence, bare-key handling, encoding and path/stream selection on duplicate-free input. Do not close a caller-owned stream, and support readable non-seekable streams. Default strict=False retains all existing duplicate/interpolation semantics and the current command-line behavior. Do not change dependency declarations or package versions.

Add maintained tests for the APIs and constructor, precise source locations, export/quoted/bare keys, strict validation before I/O, disabled loading, multiline values, invalid bindings, first-error ordering, non-seekable stream ownership, interpolation compatibility and atomic environment behavior. Update public type annotations and user-facing documentation with strict usage, exception fields and the atomicity guarantee. Add a runnable offline examples/strict_duplicates.py that requires no arguments or network, demonstrating both a successful strict load from a stream and catching a duplicate error without exposing values. Run the complete original pytest suite, the added tests and the actual example. Report actual outcomes and any remaining limitations. Do not publish or commit.
